journal: Input path plus .jsonl. First line exactly {kind:header,schema:m31-fixed96-journal-v1,specId:<id>}; then one {kind:record,row:<full record>} per case in final order; last line {kind:complete,records:1488}. All journal rows must equal final records. fsync every32 records and at header/completion; partial journal retained on failure, no retry.
sourceSha256Meaning: SHA256 of each named source file; must match source manifest and current file bytes, not trusted self-report alone
ids: bits-INDEX for fromBits; square-INDEX and sqrt-INDEX for each interval; OP-INDEX for each of all 256 pairs in specification order (48 explicit then 208 generated). INDEX is zero-based decimal without padding.
fromBitsInput: one-element array containing lowercase 16-digit hex string
intervalInput: array of one or two objects with exactly l and u fields, each a signed decimal integer string; endpoints denote integer/2^96
failureResult: object with exactly one field status

statuses.invalid-nonfinite: fromBits exponent bits are all ones (NaN or either infinity)
statuses.unresolved-domain: div denominator interval contains zero, or sqrt input lower endpoint is negative
statuses.unresolved-range: exact outward lattice endpoint falls outside [-2^352,2^352]
statuses.unresolved-iteration: sqrt reaches iteration cap; must count as qualification failure in this fixed valid suite
statuses.unresolved-sqrt-check: sqrt final exact floor-root verification fails; must count as qualification failure
statuses.invalid-bits: malformed input; not expected in the fixed suite and is qualification failure
statuses.invalid-interval: malformed/reversed input; not expected in the fixed suite and is qualification failure

precedence: Validate operands, then domain condition, then exact outward endpoint range. All generated interval operands are valid. fromBits rejects exponent-all-ones before conversion/range.
inputUnchanged: must be true for every record; runner compares serialized operands before/after and uses frozen operand objects
expectedEndpointRule: Successful endpoints must equal the tight outward lattice image for the declared operation, not merely contain it. Independent inclusion checks are also required. This makes one-unit endpoint mutation a valid negative control.
